papers.title: A comparative study on the corrosion resistance of Ti-6Al-4V produced via material extrusion and other additive manufacturing technologies
papers.abstract: This study investigated the influence of process-induced surface features, porosity, and microstructure on the corrosion behavior of Ti-6Al-4V alloy produced by different additive manufacturing (AM) technologies, including emerging sinter-based material extrusion (MEX), well-established electron beam melting (EBM) and laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), and wrought reference material. The investigated manufacturing routes produced sensibly different surfaces, porosity, and microstructures. Potentiodynamic and potentiostatic polarization tests in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) revealed stable passivity and excellent corrosion performance for all AM alloys, both in the as-built and polished conditions. After polishing, modest variations were detected among manufacturing technologies, suggesting a possible deleterious effect of the intrinsic porosity once exposed to the environment. Immersion tests performed in neutral and acidified isotonic solutions highlighted the onset of selective corrosion phenomena between the α and β phases under deoxygenated acidic conditions, consistent with Volta potential measurements. Long-term immersion in acidified isotonic solution confirmed the detrimental influence of porosity on the corrosion behavior of Ti-6Al-4V, especially for the MEX-produced alloy, where the presence of a macro-defect network promoted localized corrosion propagation.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究Ti-6Al-4V的耐腐蚀性而非力学性能，与后处理对疲劳/机械性能的影响无关。
llm.why_not_core: No mechanical testing (fatigue or tensile) results; the study focuses on corrosion resistance, not mechanical performance; does not evaluate post-processing effects on mechanical properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较不同增材制造技术生产的Ti-6Al-4V的耐腐蚀性能。
summary_zh.method: 通过动电位极化、恒电位极化和浸泡实验分析表面特征、孔隙率和微观组织的影响。
summary_zh.result: 所有增材制造合金在抛光前后均表现出良好钝化，但孔隙率会促进局部腐蚀。
summary_zh.validation: 实验验证，包括电化学测试和长期浸泡。

summary_en.motivation: This study compares the corrosion resistance of Ti-6Al-4V produced by different additive manufacturing technologies, including material extrusion, electron beam melting, and laser powder bed fusion.
summary_en.method: Potentiodynamic polarization, potentiostatic polarization, and immersion tests were conducted to analyze the effects of surface features, porosity, and microstructure on corrosion behavior.
summary_en.result: All additive-manufactured alloys exhibited stable passivity in both as-built and polished conditions, but intrinsic porosity promoted localized corrosion, especially in the material extrusion alloy.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation via electrochemical testing and long-term immersion in acidified isotonic solutions.

papers.title: Reinforced scan: a reinforcement learning enabled optimal laser scan path planning in laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Additive Manufacturing is an innovative technology that fabricates parts layer by layer. However, in Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF), printed metal parts often exhibit residual stresses, deformations, and other defects due to non-uniform temperature distribution during the printing process. To mitigate these issues, an optimized scan sequence within each layer can improve thermal uniformity. Traditional optimization methods, which rely on domain knowledge and employ trial-and-error or heuristic approaches, often fail to achieve optimal solutions due to the complex nature of the problem. One major challenge in improving scan strategies lies in the vast search space required to optimize the scan sequence for individual scan tracks within each layer, making it difficult to identify the best solution. To overcome this challenge, this work proposes an innovative scan strategy, Reinforced Scan, that leverages reinforcement learning to intelligently determine the optimal scan sequence. The method introduces a novel reward function that accounts not only for temperature variance but also for the spatial uniformity of the temperature field. By structuring the optimization problem into multiple hierarchical levels, the approach significantly reduces computational demand and enhances the manageability of the optimization process. The effectiveness of the proposed Reinforced Scan is validated through Netfabb™ Local Simulation and real-world laser scanning experiments on a Ti-6Al-4V thin plate. Its performance is compared against conventional heuristic scan sequences. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that Reinforced Scan achieves superior outcomes, notably reducing residual stress compared to traditional methods.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及Ti-6Al-4V的LPBF工艺优化，但未提供力学性能或疲劳数据，因此与用户关注的力学与疲劳性能方向关联不大。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on scan path optimization for thermal uniformity and residual stress reduction, but does not present any mechanical/fatigue performance data (tensile, fatigue life, S-N curves, etc.) that are the core of the L1 direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 针对LPBF中热不均匀导致的残余应力问题，提出强化学习优化扫描路径。
summary_zh.method: 提出Reinforced Scan策略，使用分层奖励函数考虑温度方差和空间均匀性。
summary_zh.result: 仿真和实验证明该方法有效降低残余应力。
summary_zh.validation: 通过Netfabb仿真和Ti-6Al-4V薄板激光扫描实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To mitigate residual stresses caused by non-uniform temperature distribution in LPBF, a reinforcement learning-based scan path optimization is proposed.
summary_en.method: The Reinforced Scan strategy introduces a hierarchical reward function that accounts for both temperature variance and spatial uniformity of the temperature field.
summary_en.result: Both Netfabb simulation and real-world laser scanning experiments on Ti-6Al-4V thin plates demonstrate that Reinforced Scan reduces residual stress compared to heuristic scan sequences.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed using Netfabb local simulation and experimental laser scanning with residual stress measurements on Ti-6Al-4V.

papers.title: Towards free-machining titanium: role of boron and lanthanum hexaboride in Ti-6Al-4V
papers.abstract: Many titanium alloys are notoriously difficult to machine materials, and there is a need to understand new ways to improve their machinability. This study explores the effect of trace element additions, specifically boron (B) and lanthanum hexaboride (LaB6), on the machinability of Ti-6Al-4V (Ti-64). Alloys containing these additives were prepared via casting and evaluated through slot milling tests to assess cutting forces, tool wear, chip morphology, and surface quality. The addition of boron led to the formation of titanium boride (TiB) particles, which contributed to high cutting forces, increased built-up edge (BUE) formation, and irregular chip segmentation. Conversely, LaB6 additions led to the formation of both TiB and La-rich particles, where the La-rich particles enhanced material flow, resulting in reduced cutting forces, uniform chip formation, and improved machined surface quality. These findings offer valuable insights into the design of free-machining titanium alloys and may facilitate more efficient manufacturing of Ti-64 components.

llm.relevance_to_user: 不涉及增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理工艺。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not concern post-processing of AM Ti-6Al-4V; it investigates alloy composition modifications (boron and LaB6) to improve machinability via casting, not additive manufacturing post-processing.

summary_zh.method: 通过铸造添加硼或六硼化镧，进行槽铣测试评估。
summary_zh.result: 硼添加增加切削力，六硼化镧降低切削力并改善表面质量。
summary_zh.validation: 通过槽铣实验验证切削力、刀具磨损和表面质量。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to improve the machinability of Ti-6Al-4V by adding trace elements.
summary_en.method: Boron and lanthanum hexaboride were added to Ti-6Al-4V via casting, and slot milling tests were performed to evaluate cutting forces, tool wear, chip morphology, and surface quality.
summary_en.result: Boron addition increased cutting forces and built-up edge formation, while LaB6 addition reduced cutting forces and improved chip formation and surface quality.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through slot milling tests on cast alloys.
